jet_list.title: F-15I
jet_list.desc: Israel's advanced long-range strike jet, built for heavy bombs on hardened targets.

notes: Every F-15 (type 110) with Extras "F-15 version" on Ra'am, the player's and the AI's (docs/f15i.md). Today's upgraded F-15I (the user's decision 2026-11-02); the F-15E's figures where the F-15I has none, labelled F-15E.
notes.label: the TSD's selected-unit label
notes.fm: the flight-model type (iaf_flight::data_set TYPES / REAL): its real row on the F-15's section
notes.engine_spool: F100-PW-229, F-15E: idle -> maximum afterburner in less than 4 s (USAF fact sheet), the afterburner's first segment lighting just above idle in a snap acceleration (TO 1F-15E-1): idle -> military 3.0 s as the F100-PW-220 (NASA TM-4320, inferred for the -229), light-off 0, fill 0.9 s (inferred); docs/f15i.md §1
notes.model: every F-15's model, with Models on Original too, when setup made it (under assets/, as the F-15C)
notes.radar: no row of its own: the F-15's mode table (row 0; no source gives the APG-70's modes a ratio to the APG-63's)
notes.radar.km: AN/APG-70I: fighter-sized targets at 56 NM = 104 km (Aviation Week 2010, via Wikipedia; docs/f15i.md §2)
notes.radar.ai_nm: the AI's sensor range: the 40 NM of every AI jet x 104 / 135 (the APG-70I's km against the F-15's Real 135 km), as the Sufa's 40 x 1.3
notes.gun_rounds: F-15E: M61A1, 500 rounds (USAF fact sheet); the F-15I's own count is open
notes.weapons.arm_art: its own Arming art, x_f15i (arm/arm.json; the front view setup renders from the model)
notes.weapons.loads: modern_weapons.gd record id -> [count, stations A..I] (docs/f15i.md §3): Python 5 two per wing pylon as the F-15's AIM-9L (IAF photos, April 2024); GBU-31(V)3 (BLU-109 JDAM) on the wing pylons B / H and the CFT stations C, D, F, G: six per jet (June 2025 photos; September 2024 analysis); SPICE 1000 a pair on the wing pylons B / H, as on the Baz (The War Zone 2026; the F-15I's own stations inferred)
